threads.thread_goal: Align on MVP scope, success metrics, and responsibilities.

messages.text: Team, welcome to the official kickoff for the Unified Self-Service Support Portal project! The goal is a lean MVP in 30 days to help our customers and reduce call volume. I've created a draft scope document, A1, to get us started. Please review it today so we can align on the core feature set and success metrics. This directly relates to T1.

Thanks for kicking this off. The scope in A1 looks solid for an MVP. My main recommendation is to stick strictly to reusing the existing auth and CRM systems as stated. Building new integrations would be a major risk to the 30-day timeline. Let's keep the technical scope tight.
Great! I've read A1. For content, are we focusing only on a core set of FAQs for the MVP, or should I plan for how-to guides and other article types as well?

Looks good. On the design side, to meet the deadline, I suggest we focus on a clean, functional UI based on our existing brand guidelines rather than creating a completely new visual identity. We can enhance it post-launch.
Good question. Let's stick to the top 20-25 FAQs initially. We can add how-to guides to the post-launch backlog. Agree on the UI approach as well @75507, function over form for the MVP.
This is exciting. From the front lines, I can tell you customers often ask for their case history. Would it be possible to include a 'My Cases' page in the portal? It would deflect a lot of calls.

That's a great feature idea, but it would require a deep, two-way integration with the CRM that's likely out of scope for a 30-day MVP. It introduces significant technical risk. I recommend we add it to the top of the post-launch backlog.
I agree with @472507. Excellent suggestion @6370, but let's park it for now to protect the timeline. I've added it to our post-MVP ideas list.
I have a question about A1. When we say 'non-MVP items', does that mean we won't ever build them, or just not right now?
It means 'not right now'. We'll maintain a backlog of all requested features and prioritize them for future releases after the MVP is live and we have some data.

Okay, let's formalize this. Based on the discussion, we are locking in the MVP scope as defined in A1, focusing on: 1. Core FAQ/Search, 2. Simple, responsive UI, 3. Re-use of existing systems. All other features like 'My Cases' are officially parked for post-launch consideration.
Sounds good. What about success metrics? A1 suggests 'call deflection' and 'portal usage'. Are we agreed on those two as our primary KPIs?
I'd also like to track search effectiveness. Something like 'searches with no results' or 'searches that lead to a successful article view'. This helps us improve the content.
How do we measure call deflection? Is it an estimate?
Initially, it's an estimate based on portal usage for topics that are major call drivers. We can refine it later by adding a 'Did this solve your problem?' feedback button on articles.
Excellent point. Let's set our three primary success metrics as: 1. Call Deflection Rate (estimated), 2. Portal Active Users, and 3. Search Success Rate. I'll update A1 to reflect this.
Okay, I understand the scope and metrics now. Thank you.

Perfect. With scope and metrics locked, the next immediate step is to identify the content. @6370, can you please start on T2 and pull the data on top call drivers? Let's aim to have a draft list by tomorrow.

threads.thread_goal: Prioritise top call drivers and confirm initial FAQ set.

messages.text: Hi team, as requested for T2, I've analyzed the support logs from the last 3 months. I've put the top call reasons into this sheet, A2. Let me know what you think for the initial FAQ topics.

Thanks @6370! This is a great start. I'm looking at A2 now. I can see some clear themes: billing questions, password resets, and service status. I can start drafting content for these right away. I think we can group some of the billing ones together.

Excellent, thank you for pulling this data. This is exactly what we need to ensure the portal addresses real user problems. To keep the MVP focused, let's select the top 15 from this list for our initial content set. @561463, can you and @6370 work together to highlight the 15 you'd recommend we start with in A2?

Looking at the list in A2, items like 'Check my account balance' and 'Update payment method' will require API calls to the billing system. We need to confirm the latency and reliability of those endpoints. Let's prioritize FAQs that don't require real-time data first, if possible, to de-risk the development.
Sure, I can help highlight them. What does highlight mean? Like, change the color of the row?
Yes, exactly! I can handle that. I'll highlight the 15 we think are best for static content, keeping @472507's point in mind. I'll ping you when it's ready for a final look.

Okay, @59590 and @6370, I've highlighted our recommended 15 topics in A2. They are all addressable with static content for now, avoiding the integration risk @472507 mentioned. These will be our initial set for the MVP.

Perfect, the list looks great. This is our approved FAQ set for launch. Now for ownership. @561463, it seems you'll be the primary author for most of these. Let's formally assign you as the owner for all 15 in A2 for now to get T7 started. @6370, you will be the primary reviewer for accuracy.
Sounds good. I'll add an 'Owner' column to A2 and put my name. I'll start drafting the first batch this afternoon for T7.
Happy to review them for accuracy. Just let me know when they are ready.
This list will help me finalize the information architecture. I can create categories like 'Account & Billing', 'Technical Issues', etc.
Do you need me to build the page to show the FAQs yet?
Not just yet. We need to finalize the IA and design from @75507 first. We'll get to the implementation tasks T5 and T9 after that.
Great alignment everyone. Next up is design. @75507, please share the draft IA and wireframes when you're ready to kick off T3.

threads.thread_goal: Lock in information architecture, UX approach, and visual style.

messages.text: Alright everyone, I've put together the initial Information Architecture and user flows for the portal. You can find the document in A4. It covers the main navigation, search journey, and the FAQ page structure. This is the first draft for T3, looking forward to your feedback!
Thanks @75507, this looks really clear. I like the proposed categories. Will there be a way to feature a 'top 5' or 'most popular' FAQ section on the homepage?
Yes, absolutely. I've included a component for that on the homepage wireframe in A4. We can either set that manually at first or have it be data-driven later on.

I'm looking at the user flow for searching. After a user searches, the results are on a new page. From a customer perspective, they might get confused if they can't find their answer and want to submit a support ticket. Is the 'Contact Us' link clearly visible on the search results page?
That's a great point, @6370. I had it in the footer, but I'll make it more prominent, maybe as a secondary call-to-action on the results page itself. I'll update the wireframe in A4.
For the navigation, what html tag should I use? Is it a nav or a div?

@448709, you should use the semantic `<nav>` tag for the main navigation. This is important for accessibility. Speaking of which, @75507, the flows in A4 look good, but let's make sure all interactive elements have clear focus states and that the color contrast meets WCAG AA standards as per our guidelines in A3.

Will do. I'm designing with accessibility in mind from the start. I'll add annotations to the wireframes regarding focus states and I'm using a color checker to validate against A3. The design will also be fully responsive for mobile and tablet.

This is great collaboration. It sounds like we have a clear path forward on the UX. Based on the feedback and @75507's updates, are we ready to approve the navigation structure and user flows as documented in A4?
And to formally confirm the requirements discussed: the portal must be fully mobile responsive and meet WCAG AA accessibility standards. This is a hard requirement for launch.
Confirmed. I'll finalize the visual style guide based on this and share it to cover T8. Then @448709 will have everything needed for the front-end build.
Ok, I will wait for the style guide.
Excellent. While design is being finalized, it's a good time to define the technical backbone. @472507, can you prepare the draft architecture plan for T4?
Already on it. I'll have a draft of A5 ready for review tomorrow morning.

threads.thread_goal: Confirm technical architecture, integrations, and analytics setup.

messages.text: Morning team. As promised, here is the draft Technical Architecture and Integration Plan (A5). It outlines the front-end framework, the integration points for auth/CRM, and our approach for the search service. This covers T4. I've also included a preliminary plan for analytics tracking (T10) which will feed our dashboard A7. Please review and share any questions or concerns.

Thanks @472507, this is comprehensive. The plan to use our existing authentication service is perfect, minimizes risk. Regarding analytics in A7, can you confirm we'll be able to segment portal usage by customer type? That would be very valuable for the business stakeholders.

Yes. Once the user is authenticated, we'll have access to their segment token. I've included a custom event property in the plan in A5 to capture this. We can definitely build that into the A7 dashboard.
I'm reading A5. For the search API, it says to use the GET method. Should I pass the search term as a query parameter?

Correct. The endpoint will be something like `/api/search?q={searchTerm}`. The full spec for the search service is linked in A5. Let's take any more detailed implementation questions to a separate chat to keep this thread focused on the high-level architecture.
The architecture seems straightforward and supports the UX we've designed. No concerns from my side.

Seeing no major objections, I propose we approve the technical architecture and integration approach as laid out in A5. This will unblock @448709 to start on the initial front-end implementation (T5) and the search functionality (T9).

Agreed and approved. Let's also finalize the analytics piece. The key events listed in A5 (page_view, search_performed, article_view, feedback_submitted) seem right for the MVP. We should plan to review the A7 dashboard weekly for the first month post-launch. Does that cadence work for everyone?

Weekly works perfectly. It will give us enough data to spot trends without being overwhelming. So, to confirm, we agree on the analytics events defined in A5 and a weekly reporting cadence post-launch using dashboard A7.
Ok I will start on T5. I will begin with the basic page structure.
This is great. Knowing what analytics we're tracking will help me write more effective content too.

Excellent. With these decisions made, the technical path is clear. @448709, please prioritize T5 first to get the basic pages and navigation built, then move onto T9 for the search implementation. I'll be available to support you on the integration points.

threads.thread_goal: Plan pre-launch checks, training, and go-live date.

messages.text: Hi all, as we get closer to the end of the 30-day window, I've drafted a pre-launch checklist to ensure we have everything covered for a smooth go-live. You can see it in A6. It includes content review, UX checks, and technical readiness. This is a starting point for T12. Let's refine this and set a target launch date.

This is fantastic, @561463, very proactive. This looks great. I'd like to add a section for 'Support Team Readiness'. I'm working on the training materials for T11, and we need to make sure we schedule a training session for the call centre team before we go live. I'll add a line item for that in A6.
Good checklist. From a technical standpoint, I'll add 'Final security scan' and 'Load testing on search API' to A6. We can't go live without those.
Thanks for thinking about the training. It would be really helpful for us to have a hands-on session with the portal before it goes live so we know what customers will see.

Great additions. I've updated A6. This also brings up the topic of post-launch maintenance. I've documented the content governance workflow in A8, which outlines how we'll keep articles up-to-date. This is related to T6. We need to make sure content owners are ready to follow this process from day one.
I am almost done with the front end pages. The search is still in progress.
@448709 Can you give a more specific update? What percentage of T9 is complete and do you have an ETA for when it will be ready for testing?
I think maybe 60%? I should have it ready for testing in two days.

Okay, let's use this finalized checklist in A6 as our official go-live readiness criteria. We will do a final check-in against this list 3 days before our target launch date. This reconfirms our MVP scope and ensures we haven't let anything creep in.

Perfect. And regarding A8, I'll be the primary content owner for the initial set of articles. I'm ready to maintain them after launch. @6370, as the subject matter expert, you'll continue to be the reviewer for any updates to those articles. This confirms our content maintenance plan is in place.
Yes, I can do that.
Given the remaining work, let's target a go-live date of next Friday. That gives @448709 time to finish development and gives us a few days for testing and training.

Next steps: I will finalize the training deck for T11 and schedule the session. @561463, please schedule the final content and UX review (T12) for early next week. @472507, please coordinate the final technical checks with @448709.
